messages:
oliver: Heads-up — after the cluster maintenance this morning we're seeing a slow trickle of tiny GPU pods stuck pending on a few nodes even though overall free GPU slots exist. Seems like graceful-drain + nodeLabel affinity is creating a fragmentation island.

maria: Can you paste the pending pod nodeSelector/affinity?

oliver: quick snippet: 
```
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: tiny-infer-01
spec:
  nodeSelector:
    gpu-type: a100
  affinity:
    podAntiAffinity:
      requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution:
        - labelSelector:
            matchExpressions:
              - key: app
                operator: In
                values: [inference]
          topologyKey: kubernetes.io/hostname
  resources:
    limits:
      nvidia.com/gpu: 0.125
```

kevin: 0.125 GPU requests — fractional packing is our usual culprit. What do the node allocatables look like on the affected nodes?

oliver: Most of the nodes have small residual fragments ~0.0625–0.25 GPU leftover after drains. Scheduler refuses to pack because anti-affinity with app label + host topology forces single-pod-per-host rule.

anita: Are these nodes from the warm pool? They sometimes get tainted during maintenance and the controller doesn't untaint right away, leaving warp pockets.

oliver: Yes, warmpool -> cordon -> drain -> uncordon flow. A few nodes stayed cordoned during the rolling update and then got uncordoned with leftover ephemeral PVCs. Those PVCs meant our pods had local storage affinity so scheduler kept them pinned.

raj: Could be two interacting things: (1) our graceful-drain default is --pod-deletion-timeout=5m and (2) kube-scheduler's scoring penalizes hosts with existing pods w/anti-affinity. Combined, the controller ends up evicting but not coalescing.

kevin: Short term: can we manually drain the small leftover pods and let the controller redeploy onto denser hosts? Might need to force-delete with --grace-period=0 for the tiny pods. Risk: interrupts live inferences for a few customers.

maria: We should avoid force-delete customer-facing inferences. Which teams are impacted? Any SLA hit?

oliver: Only internal test traffic and a small set of low-priority batch jobs — no customer SLA. I can force-delete the tiny-infer-* group in staging and watch packing.

anita: Longer-term we need a scheduler-level fix: either allow fractional GPU packing to co-locate multiple fractional pods per host despite anti-affinity OR introduce a coalescer admission webhook that rewrites anti-affinity for low-priority tiny pods during drain windows.

raj: I prefer a scheduler plugin change: adjust inter-pod-affinity scoring to not be absolute for tiny GPU pods (threshold by resource request). Add an override: if requested GPUs < 0.5 and pod priority < X, treat anti-affinity as soft.

kevin: We tried softening podAntiAffinity in canary months ago and it improved packing but increased noisy-neighbor risk. Need telemetry: per-node latency spikes under dense fractional packing.

maria: Can infra run a density test: re-schedule tiny pods onto a handful of nodes and collect gpu-util, host-cpu, and tail latency for model inferences. Put a canary tag.

oliver: I'll script a canary job. Plan: pick 3 nodes, drain others of tiny pods, ``kubectl apply`` 50 tiny pods with priorityClass=low and label canary=densepack. Measure 30m.

infra-bot: Deploy job triggered: canary/densepack/1754444444 (50 pods) — status: queued.

raj: Also add an experiment to change graceful-drain timeout to 30s for the warmpool controller for low-priority nodes. That reduces residual fragments.

anita: Note: changing drain timeout risks leaving orphaned PVs. We must combine with PV cleanup job.

kevin: Action items: (1) oliver force-delete staging tiny pods and run canary script (2) infra: run density telemetry on canary nodes and report perf (3) raj + scheduler team draft small change to affinity scoring and run scheduler plugin A/B canary.

maria: Can we also add an immediate mitigation: a periodic "fragment coalescer" job that attempts to pack fractional pods by temporarily relaxing anti-affinity labels for eligible pods for up to 10m? Less invasive than scheduler change.

oliver: I can prototype that as a controller that patches pods with an annotation to downgrade required -> preferred for anti-affinity if they meet filters (priority, gpu request, label).

raj: Great. Keep the rollout to low-priority namespaces first. Sync up tomorrow 10:30 with scheduler/serving/runtime teams to review telemetry.

maria: Thanks — ticketing this: infra-1527 (fragment-coalesce canary) and assign to oliver. :thumbsup:

oliver: Filed infra-1527 and started the canary. Will post results in this thread.

infra-bot: canary/densepack/1754444444 started at 1754444540

oliver: initial note: 10/50 pods scheduled onto dense nodes within 2m, kernel-level gpu memory contended but p95 latency within 2x baseline. Posting graphs in #eng-monitoring when available.
